A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OFA-TAD work. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and equations, algorithms, tables, and figures can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 34 target datasets, including baseline comparisons, component and synthesis ablations, context-size experiments, and source-dataset scaling.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds an original source-combination robustness experiment in Appendix G and Table 7.

M1.justification: The multi-view distance encoding, MoE scoring, four anomaly-synthesis strategies, MSE objective, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. Newly specified model dimensions and training parameters document the existing implementation rather than establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven source and 34 target datasets, with unchanged dataset inventories in Tables 3–4. The new experiment resamples existing sources; explicitly identifying ADBench adds provenance, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same nine baselines: LOF, KNN, IForest, DSVDD, AE, MCM, LUNAR, DRL, and DisentAD. No comparator is added or removed from the reported experiments.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds evaluation over randomly selected source subsets of sizes 2–5, extending the retained first-k source ordering studied in Section 4.6. Existing splits, metrics, and baseline protocols remain unchanged; newly disclosed training settings do not establish that earlier experiments were changed.

E4.justification: The new Appendix G tests sensitivity to source-dataset identity, addressing a question not resolved by v1's fixed-order scaling experiment. Existing component ablations, synthesis ablations, context-size studies, and gating analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 7 adds explicit means, standard deviations, and valid-trial counts of 21, 30, 30, and 21 for source sizes 2–5. Earlier uncertainty bands remain unchanged. The new prose says 30 trials per size, leaving its relationship to the two 21-trial entries imprecisely explained.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports mean AUROC values of 82.44%, 82.74%, 82.85%, and 82.98% for source sizes 2–5. All existing table values and figure results are retained, including overall AUROC/AUPRC/F1 of 0.8345/0.6629/0.6352. These are additional results under source-subset settings, not improved scores for the original comparison.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, Equations 1–10, and Appendix C's testing-time complexity analysis are unchanged. No substantive mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same novelty, transfer without target-specific retraining, comparative performance, and source-scaling claims. The additional robustness evidence does not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly interprets low variability as evidence against dependence on a lucky source configuration, and Section 4.6 adds a robustness-to-source-selection statement. Section 3.1 also adds an explanation linking transformation preferences to heterogeneous tabular structure. Existing limitations and impact discussion are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies 15 epochs, Adam, learning rate 5e-4, weight decay 2e-5, no scheduler, K=80, 128-dimensional embeddings, and two-layer experts with hidden dimension 64. v1 leaves these values unspecified. Dataset provenance is clarified; the existing code link is merely relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds tabular-learning references such as Beyazit, Grinsztajn, and Shwartz-Ziv and Armon, plus several graph and multi-agent references, while removing Pang et al. (2021). New Section 5 summarizes the largely retained Appendix A positioning; the central OFO-versus-OFA distinction is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a main-text Related Work summary, acknowledgements, and Appendix G, with corresponding section renumbering. It moves the code link into the abstract and updates the publication footer. Most existing prose remains unchanged apart from targeted explanatory and implementation additions.

P2.justification: v2 adds the four-row source-combination Table 7, moves Table 2 from page 7 to page 8, and rearranges appendix material. The previous ablation Tables 7–9 become Tables 8–10. All ten existing figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The newly disclosed training and model settings improve reproducibility, while Appendix G provides useful evidence beyond v1's fixed-order source-scaling study. The method and established benchmark results remain unchanged. The new study is limited to the original seven-source pool and has imprecise trial-count wording, but these qualifications do not outweigh the modest gains in documentation and empirical support.
